analysis_trace: Trial NCT07702890 is a first-in-human Phase 1/2a study of GUB-UCN2, a long-acting urocortin-2 analog. The trial has 3 parts: single ascending dose (SAD), multiple ascending dose (MAD), and multiple dose (MD) up to 16 weeks. Expected completion is December 2028, with SAD data expected H1 2027 per Gubra press release.

Primary endpoint is treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) over 22 weeks. Secondary endpoints are PK parameters: AUC(0-inf), AUC(0-last), tmax, Cmax for single dose (week 6) and steady-state (week 22).

Evidence sources retrieved: (1) ClinicalTrials.gov protocol for NCT07702890 - confirms trial design, endpoints, population; (2) Gubra press release (July 28, 2026) - confirms trial initiation, 188 participants, 3-part design, expected SAD data H1 2027; (3) PeptideDeck analysis (August 2026) - describes mechanism, preclinical data, fatty-acid modification for long half-life; (4) Nature Communications 2023 (PMC10319809) - UCN2 mechanism via CRHR2, acute vs chronic effects on insulin sensitivity.

Drug/mechanism: GUB-UCN2 is a fatty-acid-modified urocortin-2 analog, selective CRHR2 agonist. Native UCN2 has short half-life (minutes); Gubra's modification enables once-weekly subcutaneous dosing. Preclinical data in aged DIO rats showed 14% lean mass increase, 22-33% fat mass reduction, improved glucose/insulin.

Evidence-role assessment: No direct human PK or safety data available (trial ongoing). Preclinical rat data provides mechanism/direction but cannot support precise numeric PK predictions. Similar peptide drugs (long-acting fatty-acid modified peptides like semaglutide, tirzepatide) show predictable PK profiles with tmax 8-24h, half-life enabling weekly dosing.

Safety prediction: First-in-human peptide drugs typically show dose-proportional exposure. TEAEs expected to be manageable; most common for subcutaneous peptides are injection site reactions, GI events. Serious safety signals would likely cause early termination. No specific safety concerns from preclinical data.

PK prediction: Long-acting fatty-acid modified peptides typically show: tmax 12-48h, half-life 5-7 days enabling weekly dosing. AUC and Cmax dose-proportional. Steady-state achieved by week 4-6. Specific numeric predictions highly uncertain without human data.
Primary uncertainty: No human data available; all predictions extrapolate from preclinical models and class knowledge. Rat-to-human translation for body composition effects historically unreliable.
Confidence levels adjusted for evidence gaps: Safety endpoint moderate confidence (class knowledge); PK endpoints low-moderate confidence (mechanism-based extrapolation).
